Le Havre : un Système d'information géographique permet d'optimiser l'administration de cette gigantesque infrastructure portuaire

2026-07-13 François Ploye (Cahiers Techniques du Bâtiment) SIG, GIS, ArcGIS, Esri, 3D, Haropa Port, Le Havre, port infrastructure, BIM, GMAO, SAP, maintenance, exploitation
Read the source article

Quick summary

Haropa Port's GIS team at Le Havre has transitioned to 3D GIS using Esri's ArcGIS, improving exploitation, maintenance, and administration of France's largest port complex by integrating BIM models and enterprise systems.

Key takeaways

  • Haropa Port — combining Le Havre, Rouen, and Paris river port — is France's largest port, with its Le Havre GIS team using ArcGIS to manage the complex infrastructure
  • The team transitioned from 2D to 3D GIS in recent years, enabling better visualisation and management of port infrastructure in perpetual evolution
  • The 3D GIS serves two main business domains: exploitation (port rights and client leasing) and development/maintenance, with direct SAP integration for comparing expenses and revenue by geographic zone
  • The GIS is interfaced with Coswin GMAO (Siveco) and other specialised maintenance management software, requiring consistent reference systems between GIS and GMAO
  • BIM Revit models can be consulted within ArcGIS, bridging the gap between building information modelling and geographic information systems
